record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: A semitoric system F = ( J, H) is determined, up to symplectic equivalence, by its semicla ssical joint spectrum (i.e., the collection of points (λ, ν) ∈ R2, where λ is a eigenvalue of ˆJhbar and ν is an eigenvalue of ˆHhbar, restricted to the λ-eigenspace of ˆJ, as hbar → 0). Moreover, from any such semiclassical spectrum, one can e xplicitly construct the associated semitoric system. This conjecture is now a theorem for the special cases of quantum toric integrable systems on compact 37 manifolds [49], and for semitoric integrable systems of Jaynes-Cumm ings type [149]. The problem is that it is unclear whether one of the most subtle (perhaps the most subtle) invariants of integrable systems, known as the twisting index, can be detected in the semicla ssical spectral asymptotics. If this is the case (which is very likely), then the Pelayo-V u Ngo. c inverse spectral conjecture ([187]) above will hold. An important part of the problem is to recover the Taylor series inva riant that classifies semi-global neighbourhood s of focus-focus fibers [225]. A positive solution was given in [189, 149], but the procedure was not constructive: one had to first let hbar → 0 for a regular value c near the focus-focus value c0, and then take the limit c → c0, which doesn't help computing the Taylor series in an explicit way from the spectrum.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A semitoric integrable system on a connected symplectic 4-manifold $(M,\omega)$ is a pair $F=(J,H)$ of Poisson-commuting smooth functions $\{J,H\}=0$ such that:
(i) $J$ generates an effective Hamiltonian $S^1$-action and is proper;
(ii) the map $F=(J,H):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ has only non-degenerate singularities (in the Williamson sense) with no hyperbolic blocks.

Two semitoric systems $F=(J,H)$ on $(M,\omega)$ and $F'=(J',H')$ on $(M',\omega')$ are symplectically equivalent if there exists a symplectomorphism $\varphi:M\to M'$ with $\varphi^*J' = J$ and $\varphi^*H' = f(J,H)$ for a smooth function $f$ with $\partial f/\partial H>0$.

Quantization. Assume $F$ is quantized by a pair of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical (pseudo)differential operators $(\hat J_\hbar,\hat H_\hbar)$ with principal symbols $(J,H)$. The semiclassical joint spectrum of $F$ is the collection
$$\Sigma(\hbar) := \{(\lambda,\nu)\in\mathbb{R}^2 \mid \lambda\in\operatorname{Spec}(\hat J_\hbar),\ \nu\in\operatorname{Spec}(\hat H_\hbar\!\upharpoonright_{\ker(\hat J_\hbar-\lambda)})\},$$
considered as $\hbar\to 0$.

Problem. Prove the following two statements:
(a) (Uniqueness/inverse spectral.) If two semitoric systems $F$ and $F'$ have the same semiclassical joint spectrum (in an appropriate asymptotic sense as $\hbar\to 0$), then $F$ and $F'$ are symplectically equivalent.
(b) (Constructive recovery.) Give an explicit constructive procedure that, from the semiclassical joint spectrum, produces a representative of the symplectic equivalence class of $F$, including the explicit recovery of all symplectic invariants. In particular, recover the twisting index, and provide an explicit reconstruction of the Taylor series invariant classifying a semi-global neighborhood of each focus-focus fiber — directly from the spectral data, not merely as an iterated limit (first $\hbar\to 0$ at a regular value $c$ near a focus-focus value $c_0$, then $c\to c_0$).
artifact.category_tag: semitoric integrable systems / inverse spectral theory
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has substantially resolved the conjecture: Le Floch–Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc (arXiv:2104.06704) showed one can recover the first four symplectic invariants of simple semitoric systems from the joint spectrum, and Le Floch–Vũ Ngọc (arXiv:2309.16614) showed the twisting index can also be heard, completing the qualitative inverse-spectral statement for simple semitoric systems. The fully explicit/constructive recovery of the Taylor series invariant from the spectrum (without the iterated-limit procedure) does not appear to be fully achieved in the literature, so the constructive part of the problem remains partially open.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Le Floch, Pelayo, Vũ Ngọc prove that the first four invariants of simple semitoric systems can be recovered from the joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: First four semitoric invariants recovered from spectrum.

status_evidence.title: The twisting index in semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Le Floch–Vũ Ngọc prove that the twisting index can be detected from the semiclassical joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Twisting index can be heard, completing the list of five invariants.

status_evidence.title: San Vu Ngoc - One can hear semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: From the joint spectrum of a quantum semitoric system one can construct a representative of the isomorphism class of the underlying classical system.
status_evidence.claim: The inverse spectral conjecture is essentially established for (simple) semitoric systems.
